page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m8.2xlarge is an x86_64 virtual instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning stands at 64.0 GB, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Cache resources include 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, FMA, and AES cryptographic acceleration.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage and contains zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for persistent data. Baseline networking capability is 2 Gbps. The absence of integrated NVMe drives simplifies operational statelessness but shifts storage throughput responsibilities to remote volumes.

Benchmark results place the instance consistently in the middle tier of standard compute and memory operations. Stress-ng scores show 1886.19 for single-core and 7715.37 for multi-core performance, while Geekbench registers 1417.0 single-core and 5299.0 multi-core ratings. Memory subsystems deliver 53.2 GB/sec uncached read throughput and 37.49 GB/sec write throughput. While small model LLM inference functions adequately at 169.1 tokens/sec text generation for a 135M parameter model, heavier workloads such as 7B model execution drop to 5.96 tokens/sec due to the lack of hardware acceleration.

With its generous 64 GB memory capacity, this instance offers solid cost efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise deployments that do not require high sustained compute frequencies. It is well configured for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational databases, data transformation pipelines, and general enterprise application hosting.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m8.2xlarge is an x86_64 instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor at 2.5 GHz. With 64.0 GB of system memory, it provides an expansive 8 GB per vCPU allocation alongside a 33 MB L3 cache and support for AVX-512F and AES instructions. The configuration does not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators, routing disk traffic via network attachments alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate consistent mid-tier performance across multi-core compute, compression, and memory bandwidth tests. Large language model inference on medium models shows limited throughput given the CPU-only architecture. The substantial memory footprint relative to core count delivers balanced resource efficiency for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory databases, Redis deployments, enterprise backend applications, and caching tiers.
